newsitem.title: USA: Scudder adds six mutual funds to AARP program.
newsitem.headline: Scudder adds six mutual funds to AARP program.

text.p: Scudder Stevens and Clark said it has expanded its AARP Investment Program from Scudder by adding six more mutual funds for a total of 15 funds.

The AARP Investment Program from Scudder, open to members of the American Association of Retired Persons, currently manages about $13 billion in nine Scudder funds for 600,000 households, said Scudder spokeswoman Karen Igler.

The new funds include an international stock fund, a small company stock fund, a bond fund and a yield-tilt equity index fund, Igler said. Scudder said it will also add two asset allocation funds or "funds of funds" which invest exclusively in the AARP mutual funds.
Scudder is also raising the minimum initial investment for all but three of the funds to $2,000 from $500, although investors can invest less through automatic investments, Igler said.
